name: Tiger Game.com
description: Tiger Electronics' cartridge handheld, released in the United States in September 1997. It had a touchscreen, a stylus, and organizer apps, and with a modem cartridge it could send email and browse a text-only web. It sold poorly against the Game Boy but was ahead of its time on features.

specs.media: ROM cartridges (two slots on the original model)

curiosities: It was the first video game console with a touchscreen.
It was the first handheld that could connect to the internet, using a separate cartridge and a dial-up modem.
The original model had two cartridge slots; the 1999 Pocket Pro cut it to one and ran on two AA batteries instead of four.
Its library of about 20 games included handheld versions of Resident Evil 2 and Duke Nukem 3D.
